$comment: Tier configuration for the proof-of-life demo.
Two real MCP servers, both installable with no credentials, so a stranger
can reproduce the run: `fetch` (uvx mcp-server-fetch) and `filesystem`
(npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem).
Paths in `cwd` and in `args` written as ${configDir} resolve against the
directory this file is in, not against whatever directory the client
happened to launch from. A demo that only runs from one checkout path is
not reproducible.
The tiering is the whole judgment call, so it is spelled out rather than
left to the default:
fetch.fetch          0  reads the web. Inert, and untrusted.
read_text_file       1  reads the operator's own notes.
write_file           2  external act. `path` is where it lands.
`untrusted` lists only fetch here. The operator's own notes are private, not
hostile: a tier-1 read of them is scanned for secret values -- so Tracer can
say what is leaving -- but its text is not registered as untrusted spans. In
the starter config the default is the opposite way round (everything is
untrusted), because a proxy in front of Jira and Slack cannot tell a ticket
from a phishing email. Here it can: this file is the user's own.
Decisions are written to tracer-decisions.db beside this file. Read them with
`npx tracer log`; `"store": false` turns it off.
requireTask is false here: the point of the demo is that a client which
never calls tracer_begin_task still gets the destination rule. See B1 in
docs/BRIEF-DEMO.md and `degraded` in adapters/mcp/README.md.
